family.description: This entry represents AliA and AliB from Haloferax volcanii and similar uncharacterised transmembrane proteins from archaea. Ali stands for archaeal lipoprotein biogenesis components. These proteins are important for lipoprotein lipidation as well as for for the organism's cell shape, growth and motility [[cite:PUB00162475]].
family.name: Archaeal lipoprotein biogenesis component AliA/AliB-like

history.description: Resolved PF01889/former DUF63, excluding pneumococcal Ali namesakes. Inspected Hong2025 and Hong2026 primary text and original figures; verified D4GXF7/ADE04977.2 and D4GUE1/ADE03618.1/WP_004042703.1 sequences and domain boundaries. Added nine PHENOTYPIC graphs with34 INDIRECT OBSERVED edges for tagged processing/partitioning, shared-control lipid readouts, growth, morphology, halos, endogenous proteomic distributions and HVO_1705 fractions. Preserved negative comparisons, tagged/endogenous discrepancies, inaccessible supplements and untested catalytic mechanism. Stanford metadata establish reused WT/double-mutant controls, not independent replication. Kept IN_PROGRESS; no publication or exhaustive family completion.
history.summary: Curate archaeal AliA/AliB condition-specific causal effects with distinct paralog and assay scopes.

history.description: Retained partial same-agent scientific review of nine PHENOTYPIC graphs and34 INDIRECT OBSERVED edges. Verified current projection/overlay equivalence, reference sequences and PF01889 intervals; inspected Hong2025 Figures2-5 and Hong2026 Figures2-5 with relevant text and Methods. Preserved tagged/endogenous HVO_1176 disagreement, nonsignificant AliB comparisons, residual activity/readouts and reused WT/double lipid controls identified by Stanford metadata. Supplements, exact constructs/genomes, purified catalysis and broader member coverage remain incomplete. Native NEEDS_FOLLOWUP/common pass_with_limitations; IN_PROGRESS retained. No independent endorsement, exhaustive family completion or publication.

record.description: This entry represents AliA and AliB from Haloferax volcanii and similar uncharacterised transmembrane proteins from archaea. Ali stands for archaeal lipoprotein biogenesis components. These proteins are important for lipoprotein lipidation as well as for for the organism's cell shape, growth and motility [[cite:PUB00162475]].

evidence.explanation: Original Figures3-5 and Methods establish biogenesis/physiology phenotypes; in-vitro stand-alone activity and residue tests remain future work in the Discussion. Matched and cross-complementation are reported in text,but Supplementary Figure6 was not inspected.

Original Figures2-5 distinguish broad AliA-associated changes from the narrower AliB response. AliB bulk lipid comparison(p0.077),TX distribution(p0.98) and reported aliA qPCR trend(p0.174) do not justify increase/decrease arrows. Figure3 validation counts depend on filtering and missing data,not direct lipid-peptide sequencing.

discussions.notes: Obtain readable supplements,exact inserts and mutant-genome evidence; inspect additional substrate/taxon studies. The primary qPCR control threshold printed as deltaCt<=10 and the prose ordering of WT/aliB medians remain unresolved. The866 proteins counted in the frozen family are not all functionally characterized. Preprints and database echoes are not independent experimental origins.
discussions.prompt: Resolve AliA catalytic sufficiency and AliB processing chemistry without collapsing substrate-specific observations.
discussions.rationale: Whole-gene deletions support the retained cellular effects,but do not establish purified lipid-transfer activity,lipid donor identity,AliB peptidase activity or a conserved-residue mechanism. Tagged HVO_1176 and endogenous proteomics disagree; HVO_B0139 misses a stringent proteomic threshold. These contexts cannot be merged into universal lipidation requirements.

evidence.explanation: The record identifies single-mutant YH_57/aliB and YH_113/aliA data and points H53/double-deletion data to vq241jx8767. Metadata were inspected; raw LC-MS integration was not repeated.

Current InterPro and the frozen previous-name TSV identify the archaeal family and historical DUF63 alias. Member-specific APIs verify AliA87-379 and AliB17-263; original FASTAs match the stated UniProt reference versions.

discussions.notes: Main PMC articles downloaded successfully despite browser-tool access failures. Attachment URLs returned challenge HTML or403; other official endpoints gave DNS,404 or429 failures. No missing supplement is treated as biological negative evidence. Minimal extracts,identity verification and access/coverage limits are retained under evidence/PF01889. No publication or exhaustive family review is claimed.
discussions.prompt: Preserve the shared lipid-control provenance and distinguish archaeal AliA/AliB from pneumococcal namesakes.
discussions.rationale: The2026 lipid deposit explicitly links its WT/double-deletion controls to the2025 deposit. Repeated plots must not be counted as independent replication. PF01889 is former DUF63,not pneumococcal PF00496 peptide-binding Ali proteins.
